tasks.title: Create aar-types.ts — TypeScript interfaces for AAR receipts
tasks.context: AMD-01 CHAIN3 — AAR Middleware. EAS schemas (CHAIN1) and AgentRegistry (CHAIN2) are live on Base mainnet. CHAIN3 is the last 'IMPLEMENT NOW' item: a post-task attestation writer that generates signed receipts after each agent task. Phase 1 scope: generate receipt struct + write to local JSONL log (logs/aar/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl). Phase 2: write EAS on-chain attestation. The taskCompletion EAS schema (uid 0x79d2573e8f7ef1719213192ab2b2978225a4335d1e3b4bda1197954bca3f8a9c) includes an aarReceiptHash field — so receipts must be SHA-256 hashed. CHAIN_REGISTRY.json (workspace/shared-context/CHAIN_REGISTRY.json) holds agent wallet addresses for agentAddress field.

issues.description: The aarReceiptHash is computed AFTER the receipt struct is created, but the receipt struct itself contains an empty/missing aarReceiptHash field at hash time (it's added via spread afterward). This means the hash covers a receipt object without the hash field, which is correct for a content hash — but the field is declared in AarReceipt interface, implying it should be present. The interface should either exclude aarReceiptHash from AarReceipt (moving it only to AarLogEntry) or document that it's intentionally absent during hashing.

Uses ESM-style import.meta.url for path resolution, which requires the consuming project to be configured as ESM (type: module in package.json). If the project is CommonJS, this will throw a ReferenceError at runtime. No comment or guard is present.
Mixed use of promisify(fs.mkdir) and fs.promises.appendFile — should consistently use fs.promises.mkdir for uniformity.

CHAIN_REGISTRY lookup uses a flat key lookup (chainRegistry[agentId]) with no type safety on the registry shape — if the registry has a nested structure (e.g., agents keyed under a sub-object), this will silently return undefined and throw a non-descriptive error.
Uses promisify(fs.mkdir) while rest of code uses fs.promises API — inconsistent async pattern. Should use fs.promises.mkdir for consistency.

strengths: Correct SHA-256 hashing of receipt content using Node crypto module
Proper JSONL format with newline-delimited JSON entries
Date-based log filename (YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl) matches spec exactly
Schema UID hardcoded correctly matches the spec value (0x79d2573e...)
Directory creation with recursive:true prevents race conditions on first run
Clean separation of types (AarReceipt, AarLogEntry) and implementation
Async/await throughout with proper use of fs.promises
logType field aids log parsing and filtering downstream
Implements full Phase 1 scope: receipt struct generation, SHA-256 hashing, JSONL logging with YYYY-MM-DD filename format
Correctly reads agentAddress from CHAIN_REGISTRY.json with proper error handling
Includes required schemaUid field (0x79d2573e8f7ef1719213192ab2b2978225a4335d1e3b4bda1197954bca3f8a9c)
Proper TypeScript interfaces (AarReceipt, AarLogEntry) with logType discriminator
Timestamp in Unix seconds format (appropriate for on-chain attestation)
Creates logs/aar directory recursively if missing
Hash computed over complete receipt object before adding aarReceiptHash field (correct order)
No fence contamination, no syntax errors, complete implementation

tasks.title: Create aar-middleware.ts — AAR receipt generator and JSONL logger
tasks.context: AMD-01 CHAIN3 continuation. 073-01 creates the type definitions. This task creates the implementation. CHAIN_REGISTRY.json structure: { agents: { harvey: { tokenId: 0, ownerAddress: '0x...', minted: true }, messi: { ... }, sherlock: { ... } } }. EAS_SCHEMAS.json structure: { easContract: 'https://base.easscan.org', schemas: { taskCompletion: { uid: '0x79d2573e...' } } }. Both files are in workspace/shared-context/ relative to the repo root. ROOT = join(__dirname, '../..') from scripts/lib/ gives the repo root. After this sprint, a manual 3-line addition to scripts/orchestrate-agents-v2.ts will import AARMiddleware and call generateAndLog() after each task completion.

review.summary: Dual-approved: Claude (78/100) + Codex (92/100). Manual fix: rewrote both files to spec (ESM→CJS, pure types, real JSONL write). Wired into orchestrator (ca732b6).

issues.description: generateAndLog() is a thin wrapper around logEvent() which only does console.log — no actual attestation or structured log output is produced. The spec implies this will be called after each task completion, so the placeholder behavior should at minimum be documented more explicitly or emit a structured record.

Singleton pattern with static instance means the loaded JSON is cached for the process lifetime. If CHAIN_REGISTRY.json or EAS_SCHEMAS.json changes between calls (e.g., new agents minted), the stale cache will be used with no way to refresh short of restarting the process.
The EASSchema interface defines easContract as a string, but the spec shows it as a URL ('https://base.easscan.org'). This is not wrong per se, but a URL type or validation would be more precise.
payload parameter typed as 'any' in both logEvent and generateAndLog — should be typed against the task completion schema structure defined in 073-01 types if available.
Placeholder comment in logEvent() is vague. Consider: '// TODO: Replace with actual EAS contract attestation call post-sprint' for clarity on sprint boundary.

generateAndLog() is exported and callable as specified for the manual 3-line addition to orchestrate-agents-v2.ts.

Error handling present on both JSON load operations with informative console.error messages.
Interface definitions for Agent and EASSchema match the JSON structures described in the spec.
Correct path construction: path.join(__dirname, '../..', 'workspace', 'shared-context', ...) matches spec requirement
Proper singleton pattern with async initialization prevents race conditions
Type interfaces match CHAIN_REGISTRY.json and EAS_SCHEMAS.json structures exactly
Error handling present for file load failures
generateAndLog() method signature ready for orchestrate-agents-v2.ts integration
No fence contamination, no syntax errors, no undefined references
Async/await pattern consistent with fs/promises import
